intro: A fun 10-minute journey around Kerala, India and the world. Read the stories, discover a fun fact, then take the Daily Brain Spark quiz!

slides.title: Kerala says goodbye to a beloved temple elephant
slides.summary: Pallatt Brahmadathan, a 54-year-old temple elephant known for Kerala festivals, died after being struck by lightning. He had been a familiar presence at temple festivals and had carried the sacred thidambu at Thrissur Pooram.
slides.fun: Brahmadathan was brought to Kerala from Arunachal Pradesh 28 years ago and was remembered for his calm nature.

slides.title: Rain watch continues across Kerala
slides.summary: The India Meteorological Department is warning of rain, thunderstorms and gusty winds in Kerala. Several districts, including Ernakulam, Idukki, Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram and Wayanad, are under a yellow alert for 6 October.
slides.fun: A yellow alert is a reminder to stay weather-aware and take care during heavy rain and thunderstorms.
slides.source: Kerala Kaumudi / IMD weather report, 4 Oct 2026, updated for 6 Oct

slides.title: New bridges are coming to Vaduthala
slides.summary: A current Kerala affairs report says construction of the Vaduthala railway overbridge and the Perandoor-Vaduthala bridge is set to begin on 7 October. The projects are intended to improve connections and ease travel in the area.
slides.fun: Bridges are examples of civil engineering: engineers design structures that help people cross roads, railways or water safely.
slides.source: Kerala PSC Current Affairs Brief, 6 Oct 2026

slides.title: India wins big at the Astronomy & Astrophysics Olympiad
slides.summary: India's five-member team returned from the 19th International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics in Hanoi with four gold medals and one silver. The event ran from 25 September to 5 October.
slides.fun: Astronomy studies objects and events in space, while astrophysics uses physics to understand how the universe works.

slides.title: India demonstrates a free-space quantum key link
slides.summary: India has demonstrated a 5.56-kilometre free-space quantum key distribution link between BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar. The technology explores highly secure ways of sharing encryption keys.
slides.fun: Quantum key distribution uses ideas from quantum physics to help detect attempts to secretly interfere with a key-sharing process.

slides.title: Mountain Guardian 2026 begins in Uttarakhand
slides.summary: The Indian Army's Mountain Guardian 2026 exercise began on 5 October at Chaubattia, Uttarakhand, and is scheduled through 18 October. It focuses on practising skills for high-altitude mountain conditions.
slides.fun: High-altitude areas can be cold, steep and oxygen-poor, so people working there need special training and equipment.

slides.title: A 'ghost particle' helps win the Physics Nobel
slides.summary: Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for pioneering the detection of high-energy neutrinos with the IceCube observatory at the South Pole. Neutrinos are tiny particles that rarely interact with matter.
slides.fun: IceCube uses about a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice and thousands of sensors to catch clues from neutrinos arriving from space.

people.name: Francis Halzen
people.bio: Francis Halzen is a physicist known for leading the IceCube neutrino observatory project at the South Pole.
people.why: He received the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for pioneering high-energy neutrino detection.

slides.title: Scientists honoured for using light to study the brain
slides.summary: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel received the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries that made optogenetics possible. Optogenetics lets scientists use light to control specific nerve cells.
slides.fun: The method gives researchers a precise way to switch certain nerve cells on or off and study how brain circuits work.

people.name: Karl Deisseroth
people.bio: Karl Deisseroth is a scientist and physician whose work helped develop optogenetics, a light-based method for studying nerve cells.
people.why: He shared the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

slides.title: NASA shows a giant auroral oval from space
slides.summary: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day for 6 October features a complete auroral oval observed by the SMILE spacecraft using ultraviolet light. The mission studies how the solar wind interacts with Earth's magnetic environment.
slides.fun: A complete auroral oval is too large to see as one circle from the ground, but a spacecraft high above Earth can observe it.
